item.title: Charters wins case
item.description: THE High Court in Suva has permanently stayed criminal proceedings against Charlie Charters, ruling that the prosecution brought by FICAC was an abuse of process. Charters, a former journalist, had been charged with two counts of aiding and abetting an unnamed FICAC officer in the unauthorised publication of official information on his Facebook page.
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court in Suva has permanently stayed criminal proceedings against Charlie Charters, ruling that the prosecution brought by FICAC was an abuse of process.

Charters, a former journalist, had been charged with two counts of aiding and abetting an unnamed FICAC officer in the unauthorised publication of official information on his Facebook page.

In a ruling delivered yesterday, Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu found that FICAC breached Charters’ rights under Section 13 of the 2013 Constitution by failing to properly caution him after detaining him at Nadi Airport in February and denying him the opportunity to consult a lawyer before questioning him about his journalistic sources.

The court also found that FICAC violated Charters’ rights under Section 17(4) of the Constitution, including his freedom of speech, expression and publication, and his right not to disclose confidential journalistic sources.

Justice Bulamainaivalu ruled the charges were “doomed to fail”, finding that FICAC had failed to identify the principal offender, allegedly aided and abetted by Charters.

He further found that FICAC had not properly applied the test for prosecution and instead hastily laid charges while breaching Charters’ constitutional rights, undermining the fairness of any trial.

While rejecting the defence’s challenge to the validity of Lavi Rokoika’s appointment as acting FICAC Commissioner, under the de facto officer doctrine, Justice Bulamainaivalu held that the cumulative constitutional breaches amounted to an abuse of process and permanently halted the trial, which had been scheduled for September.

item.title: High CourtconvictsCilicewa
item.description: THE High Court in Suva has convicted Anare Vuli Cilicewa of the brutal murder of Sabreen Shaheen Ali, also known as Sabrina. Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu yesterday found the State had proved the murder charge beyond reasonable doubt after considering the evidence of 10 prosecution witnesses, agreed facts and exhibits tendered during the trial.
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court in Suva has convicted Anare Vuli Cilicewa of the brutal murder of Sabreen Shaheen Ali, also known as Sabrina.

Justice Pita Bulamainaivalu yesterday found the State had proved the murder charge beyond reasonable doubt after considering the evidence of 10 prosecution witnesses, agreed facts and exhibits tendered during the trial.

In his judgment, Justice Bulamainaivalu rejected Cilicewa’s evidence, finding that he was not a credible or reliable witness.

According to evidence presented during the trial, the 28-year-old victim sustained severe injuries during an initial dispute inside a house in Raiwaqa, where she was stabbed with a broken wine bottle on September 8, 2024.

Court testimonies revealed that when an occupant of the house attempted to take Ms Ali to the hospital, Cilicewa threatened them against seeking help.

The court heard that in a subsequent attack, Cilicewa gagged Ms Ali using a condom stuffed with cloth, strangled her with an electrical cord, and bound her hands and feet.

Her body, wrapped in a white bedsheet, was later dragged to a basement room and hidden beneath a wooden bed. Police recovered the victim’s body on the evening of September 9, 2024, following a report made by the owner of the property.

The judge accepted the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, ruling that it remained credible and reliable.

Cilicewa has been further remanded in custody with a sentencing hearing scheduled for Friday next week.

item.title: Murder accused gives evidence
item.description: THE man charged with the murder of Nadi physician Dr Isireli Biumaitotoya testified at the High Court in Lautoka yesterday that the deadly fight between them was triggered by mounting distress over online social media posts targeting his family. Ratu Peceli Rosotokaicake Rokoravolo gave evidence in his defence before Justice Aruna Aluthge. He is charged with the murder of Dr Biumaitotoya in Nadi b
item.content:encoded:
THE man charged with the murder of Nadi physician Dr Isireli Biumaitotoya testified at the High Court in Lautoka yesterday that the deadly fight between them was triggered by mounting distress over online social media posts targeting his family.

Ratu Peceli Rosotokaicake Rokoravolo gave evidence in his defence before Justice Aruna Aluthge. He is charged with the murder of Dr Biumaitotoya in Nadi between August 31 and September 1, 2025.

His lawyer Losana Taukei called Mr Rokoravolo, who denied being in a relationship with Dr Biumaitotoya. He told the court their association was strictly financial, and that Dr Biumaitotoya supported his canteen business in the village and his family.

The court heard that after travelling from Mokani Village, Tailevu, to Nadi on August 30 last year to collect $1000, Dr Biumaitotoya told him to have dinner and he showered afterwards.

It was after this that an argument erupted between the two regarding Dr Biumaitotoya’s Facebook posts.

Mr Rokoravolo told the court that Dr Biumaitotoya was already consuming alcohol when he initially arrived, however, the two went to Votualevu to buy more alcohol.

He said they then travelled to Lautoka on August 31 where they bought more alcohol.

Mr Rokoravolo said that after returning to the physician’s home, Dr Biumaitotoya swore at him and pulled a cane knife from beside his bed.

During a struggle, Mr Rokoravolo said he looped an extension cord around the doctor’s neck to loosen his grip on the knife.

After retrieving the knife, Mr Rokoravolo said he asked if Dr Biumaitotoya wanted to kill him before swinging the knife, causing Dr Biumaitotoya to collapse.

Emotionally addressing the court, Mr Rokoravolo said he was not in the right state of mind to get medical help, maintaining he never intended to kill the doctor but lost control out of anger over the online posts.

Under cross-examination by State counsel Joeli Nasa, Mr Rokoravolo agreed the argument involved alleged misuse of business funds sent by Dr Biumaitotoya to him but he rejected assertions that his wife accepted the arrangement for financial gain.

Further evidence from the accused’s uncle, Josaia Boselawa and elder brother Ratu Seru Vuibau detailed public ridicule surrounding the Facebook posts, including other people’s description of Mr Rokoravolo as a homosexual.

Mr Vuibau told the court under cross examination that after confronting his brother a second time, Mr Rokoravolo admitted to being in a relationship with Dr Biumaitotoya. The defence closed its case yesterday.

Oral closing submissions will be made on August 4.

item.title: 1 million visitors
item.description: Fiji is firmly on track to lock in an unprecedented one million visitors for the 2026 calendar year. item.content:encoded:
Fiji is firmly on track to lock in an unprecedented one million visitors for the 2026 calendar year.

After surpassing the one-million mark for the 12 months to June this year, and with total year-to-date arrivals for the first half of this year sitting at 460,628 visitors, ANZ Group’s senior Pacific economist Dr Kishti Sen is “very confident” about achieving one million visitors for the actual 2026 calendar year.

“All Fiji needs to do is hold the July to December 2026 arrivals at last year’s levels (542,607 visitor arrival from July-December 2025),” Dr Sen told this newspaper.

“You don’t even have to grow those numbers. Holding is sufficient and the feedback I’m getting is that bookings to at least August are looking good.

“That means we will likely do better over July and August when compared to last year.”

Dr Sen said the growth that Fiji has had in the first six months plus expected better numbers for July and August would be enough to break the one million visitor milestone this calendar year.

“Fiji can focus on the October, November and December months of 2026 to ensure that this year’s momentum in the visitor arrival economy is carried into 2027. Very important this.”

The ANZ Group’s Pacific Insight report had revealed Fiji surpassed the one million visitor arrivals mark for the 12 months to June this year; and it also showed that cumulative arrivals to June 2026 was the highest ever when compared to the same period of previous years.

That means the January-June 2026 arrivals beat the January-June inbound demand of all previous years.

While Dr Sen could not comment on the cash yield across the industry, citing unavailability of data, he said for the 35 or so hotels surveyed by Tourism Fiji and its partners, revenue for those groups over the January to May months this year were seven to 12 per cent higher than the same months of last year.

“Stronger demand is contributing to it and that, in turn, is supporting jobs in the industry.

“The upshot is that the tourism industry is doing a remarkable job in sustaining demand, jobs and economic growth for Fiji,” Dr Sen said.

item.title: TOPEX 2026 signs on returning sponsor
item.description: TELECOM Fiji Limited (TFL) returns this year as a top-tier supporter of the upcoming 2026 Top Executive Conference (TOPEX), organised annually by the Fiji Commerce & Employers Federation (FCEF). During the announcement of the sponsorship at the FCEF Hub in Suva yesterday, TOPEX 2026 organising committee chairperson Rowena Taito said Telecom Fiji had been a sponsor for over 10 years.
item.content:encoded:
TELECOM Fiji Limited (TFL) returns this year as a top-tier supporter of the upcoming 2026 Top Executive Conference (TOPEX), organised annually by the Fiji Commerce & Employers Federation (FCEF).

During the announcement of the sponsorship at the FCEF Hub in Suva yesterday, TOPEX 2026 organising committee chairperson Rowena Taito said Telecom Fiji had been a sponsor for over 10 years.

She said last year Telecom Fiji became the platinum sponsor for TOPEX 2025 and 2026 as well.

“What we have with Telecom goes beyond just a sponsorship. They’re a true partner, so they help us shape the event,” Ms Taito said.

“So, you know, it’s a real great partnership that we have together,” she said.

Telecom Fiji chief marketing officer Saileshni Chand said supporting TOPEX was more than sponsorship; it’s an investment in leadership development, business excellence and the future prosperity.

She said Telecom Fiji’s partnership with FCEF reflected commitment to empowering businesses through connectivity, digital transformation and technology solutions that allows growth and productivity.

“As Fiji continues to navigate an increasingly digital and connected world, the need for visionary leadership, innovation and strategic partnership has never been better,” Ms Chand said.

FCEF chief executive officer Edward Bernard said this year’s event will bring together about 350 senior business officials including government ministers, permanent secretaries, international, regional and local speakers to talk and discuss issues and ways to move forward.

“These are the key ones. But what this conference will do is not only look at the problems but will look at unpacking them and seeing what the opportunities are to move forward,” Mr Bernard said.

TOPEX 2026 will be held from November 19 to 21 at the Sofitel Fiji Resort and Spa in Denarau, Nadi.

item.title: Mentorship program reaches 200 businesses
item.description: FIJI THRIVE, a business development program designed for local enterprises recently surpassed 200 graduates with its latest cohort of 27 local entrepreneurs in Sigatoka where participants completed personalised mentoring, practical workshops and networking designed to strengthen their businesses. Fiji THRIVE is a joint initiative by Bank of South Pacific (BSP) and Australian Business Volunteers (A
item.content:encoded:
FIJI THRIVE, a business development program designed for local enterprises recently surpassed 200 graduates with its latest cohort of 27 local entrepreneurs in Sigatoka where participants completed personalised mentoring, practical workshops and networking designed to strengthen their businesses.

Fiji THRIVE is a joint initiative by Bank of South Pacific (BSP) and Australian Business Volunteers (ABV).

The latest group included businesses operating in tourism, hospitality, retail, agribusiness, manufacturing, handicrafts, bakery operations and sawmilling.

BSP relieving country head Maikash Ali said the programme demonstrates BSP’s commitment to championing prosperity by empowering local entrepreneurs and supporting inclusive economic growth.

“Together with our partner, Australian Business Volunteers, we are proud to support these resilient entrepreneurs who are solving real challenges, creating opportunities and driving economic activity in their communities,” he said.

“In this latest cohort, we are especially pleased that 17 women-owned businesses participated, reinforcing our shared commitment to building a more inclusive and vibrant business community.”

Since launching in 2023, Fiji THRIVE has provided practical business capability development by combining one-on-one mentoring, interactive workshops and ongoing coaching to help entrepreneurs improve business planning, financial management, operational performance and long-term sustainability.

ABV Fiji senior program manager Ravi Chand said the program’s success is built on practical mentoring and lasting relationships.

“Our Skilled Business Professionals work alongside entrepreneurs to solve real business challenges using practical experience and tailored advice.

“Participants leave with stronger business skills, greater confidence and valuable networks that continue long after the workshops have finished.”

With the Sigatoka programme now complete, Fiji THRIVE resumes in Suva, where a new cohort of entrepreneurs will begin their business capability journey.

“Together, BSP and Australian Business Volunteers remain committed to expanding the programme’s reach and equipping more Fijians with the skills, mentoring and confidence to build stronger businesses and contribute to Fiji’s economic future,” BSP stated.

THRIVE stands for Together, Helping build a Resilient, Inclusive and Vibrant Economy.

The program combines business mentoring, practical workshops and ongoing coaching to help entrepreneurs build stronger, more resilient and sustainable businesses.

An ABV Skilled Business Professional, left, mentors a Fiji THRIVE participant. Picture: BSP/SUPPLIED

item.title: Prasad assumes club presidency
item.description: SHREEDHAR Motors national manager Sales and Marketing Arvin Prasad has assumed presidency of the Rotary Club of Suva Peninsula Sunset for the 2026-2027 Rotary year. Mr Prasad’s role in this position is to provide leadership and direction to the club while also inspiring members to service their communities through meaningful and sustainable projects.
item.content:encoded:
SHREEDHAR Motors national manager Sales and Marketing Arvin Prasad has assumed presidency of the Rotary Club of Suva Peninsula Sunset for the 2026-2027 Rotary year.

Mr Prasad’s role in this position is to provide leadership and direction to the club while also inspiring members to service their communities through meaningful and sustainable projects.

He said he would work closely with the board of directors and club members to plan and oversee community initiatives, strengthen membership and community organisations, and ensure the club operated effectively.

“My responsibility is to unite our members around a shared vision of service and ensure that the project we undertake create lasting impact on the communities we serve,” Mr Prasad told this newspaper.

“I’m deeply grateful for the trust and confidence that my fellow Rotarians have placed in me to lead the club. The role means a great deal to me because it provides an opportunity to give back to the community in a meaningful way while working alongside a passionate team of volunteers who are committed to creating positive change.

“The club, Rotarians, and the wider community can expect a leadership style that is inclusive, transparent, and focused on service. My priority is to strengthen and empower our members while building meaningful partnership with businesses and community organisations.”

Mr Prasad said while he holds a leadership position at work, serving as president of the Rotary club was unique “because it is built entirely on voluntary role”. “Unlike a corporate leadership role, success is not measured by financial performance our business outcome, but by the positive impact we make in the lives of others.”

He will serve in that role for a year from July 1 to June 30 next year.

Mr Prasad is an experienced sales and marketing professional with more than 30 years of leadership experience in the finance and automotive industries across Fiji. His current position oversees sales operations, marketing strategies, budgeting, and customer relations for branches in Suva, Lautoka, and Labasa. He began his career at Merchant Bank of Fiji (now Merchant Finance) in 1991, progressing through several roles to become a Branch Manager Labasa and Lautoka respectively. He later joined Carpenters Motors, holding senior management positions as sales manager Nadi & branch manager Lautoka before moving to Niranjans Autoport Ltd/Eurocars as sales manager and branch manager. Mr Prasad has completed numerous professional development courses in sales, marketing, leadership, corporate governance, occupational health and safety, emotional intelligence, and automotive product training in Japan, Thailand, and Australia. His key strengths include strategic sales leadership, business development, customer relationship management, team leadership, and an extensive corporate network throughout Fiji.

item.title: Fintech in finder tool
item.description: MICRO, small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) that have used the services of Business Assistance Fiji (BAF) now have access to yet another supporting service provider, local fintech ThirdRoc Finance Limited. The collaboration between BAF and ThirdRoc was launched in Suva yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
MICRO, small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) that have used the services of Business Assistance Fiji (BAF) now have access to yet another supporting service provider, local fintech ThirdRoc Finance Limited.

The collaboration between BAF and ThirdRoc was launched in Suva yesterday.

“As part of this initiative, ThirdRoc has been officially integrated into the newly launched BLP Finance Finder Tool, making it easier than ever for local businesses to navigate and secure the financial support they need to grow,” BAF said in a statement.

BAF is the in-country partner of Business Link Pacific (BLP), a private sector development programme funded by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) and delivered by DT-Global.

”BLP works with financial institutions to improve access to financial services for businesses in Fiji,” BLP director Steve Knapp said.

“We are pleased to see an increasing number of financial products supporting the private sector in the country. “Responsible and appropriate finance can be a key tool for growing businesses”

The Finance Finder platform serves as a critical digital bridge, connecting local businesses with formal financial institutions, products, and diagnostic services.

By onboarding ThirdRoc, BAF expands the ecosystem of flexible, accessible financial solutions available to entrepreneurs, particularly those striving to transition from the informal to the formal sector, according to BAF.

”We are thrilled to welcome ThirdRoc to the BLP Finance Finder platform,” BAF general manager Nitika Singh said.

“This collaboration reinforces our commitment to expanding digital and financial inclusion for all businesses in Fiji, including those outside Viti Levu and rural women entrepreneurs.”

ThirdRoc, Fiji’s first Reserve Bank Fiji (RBF)-licensed Peer-2-Peer (P2P) lender, promises to slash turnaround time for invoices to less than two days.

“Businesses that wait 60 days to get paid on invoices get most of it from us in 48 hours,” Thirdroc country head Fiji, Tawake Tui said.

“Fijian businesses wait 30, 60, sometimes 90 days for money they have already earned.

“That wait costs jobs, stock and sleep. ThirdRoc Finance Limited is being licensed by the Reserve Bank of Fiji to close that gap, so a supplier who delivers this week can be paid this week.

“For the large buyers those suppliers serve, nothing changes: same payment terms, same process, but a stronger and more reliable supply chain behind them,” Mr Tui said.

“We are proud to launch Finance Finder with Business Assistance Fiji and take this to every MSME in the country.”
